title: Quantum Cellular Automata from Kramers-Wannier Dualities and Modular Relations
abstract: Recent work has constructed higher-dimensional analogs of non-invertible symmetries similar to 1+1d Kramers-Wannier duality. Although their continuum descriptions often treat purely gravitational topological terms as inessential counterterms, these terms can have an essential lattice manifestation: they distinguish states prepared by finite-depth quantum circuits (FDQCs) from those entangled by nontrivial quantum cellular automata (QCAs). Motivated by this mismatch, we show that QCAs associated with gravitational topological responses arise in several related settings: (1) lattice realizations of projective $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z}_N)$ relations generated by topological operations on symmetries; (2) squares of dualities that generalize the relation between fermionization and Kramers-Wannier duality; (3) lattice implementations of QCAs through higher-form gauging; and (4) invertible phases protected by generalized time-reversal symmetries. We derive new projective $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z}_N)$ relations whose projective phases are gravitational topological responses constructed from Stiefel-Whitney classes. We furthermore give a general protocol for preparing the associated QCA-entangled states using finite-depth unitary circuits, measurements, and error correction. These results unify the study of gravitational topological responses in field theories, higher dimensional dualities, and quantum cellular automata.
summary: This work connects advanced concepts from algebraic topology (like Stiefel-Whitney classes) to the physics of Quantum Cellular Automata. It shows that gravitational topological responses are crucial for distinguishing true lattice entanglement from simpler circuit preparations. The findings unify several theoretical frameworks, providing a deeper understanding of topological order in quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper addresses a fundamental mismatch between continuum field theory descriptions of topological terms (which often ignore gravitational effects) and their essential, non-trivial manifestation on a discrete lattice.
main_result: It establishes that Quantum Cellular Automata (QCAs) associated with gravitational topological responses arise in four distinct physical settings, unifying the study across dualities, higher dimensions, and lattice models.
method: The authors derive new projective SL(2, Z_N) relations using gravitational topological responses constructed from Stiefel-Whitney classes and provide protocols for state preparation using finite-depth circuits.
model_or_system: The core model involves Quantum Cellular Automata (QCAs) derived from higher-dimensional analogs of Kramers-Wannier duality, analyzed via lattice realizations of projective SL(2, Z_N) relations and higher-form gauging.
key_observables: Gravitational topological responses, Ground State Degeneracy (GSD), and the comparison between states prepared by Finite-Depth Quantum Circuits (FDQCs) versus QCA entanglement.
important_parameters: The lattice dimension ($3+1$d mentioned), the symmetry group ($	ext{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z}_N)$), and the topological invariants (Stiefel-Whitney classes).
main_assumptions: Field theory often treats gravitational topological terms as inessential counterterms, an assumption contradicted by lattice physics.

paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes how gravitational topological responses manifest in four contexts: projective SL(2, Z_N) relations, dualities generalizations, higher-form gauging, and time-reversal protected phases. It builds mathematical machinery around Gauss sums to classify these responses.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous lattice framework for understanding topological invariants that are often glossed over in continuum field theory treatments of quantum matter, directly impacting how we model exotic correlated states.
